newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: China keen to boost trade ties with Latin America.
newsitem.headline: China keen to boost trade ties with Latin America.

text.p: Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng, ending a tour of Latin America, spelled out Thursday China's keen interest in boosting trade ties with the region.

Li, in Venezuela on the last stop of a nine-day Latin trip that also took him to Chile and Brazil, said China "within the framework of South-South cooperation ... regarded ties with Latin America and the Caribbean to be of the utmost importance."
The Chinese premier made the comment in an address to the Latin American Economic System (SELA), a Caracas-based regional economic think-tank actively promoting economic integration.
Li said potential areas of growth for trade between China's 1.2 billion people and Latin America's 470 million inhabitants included forestry, paper manufacturing and foodstuffs.
Among products that China can now sell to the region, Li mentioned agricultural, construction and transport machinery.

Trade between China and Latin America and the Caribbean nearly tripled in five years to reach $6 billion in 1995, SELA figures show. However, more than a third of this commerce was with Brazil, Latin America's largest and most populous country.

SELA Permanent Secretary Carlos Moneta, speaking before Li, described trade exchanges between the two blocs until the 1970s as "occasional". They were still modest, he said, and obstacles to be overcome included "communication barriers and unawareness of our respective market opportunities."
Li stressed China's interest in participating in joint ventures and mentioned such an agreement with Brazil on a $150- million project to produce Earth-monitoring satellites.
In Chile, he said China planned to invest in copper mining while in oil-rich Venezuela the Asian powerhouse signed deals on the supply of trademark boiler fuel Orimulsion.

Li also signed with Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera Wednesday a memorandum of undestanding for a feasibility study on a $320-million joint venture Orimulsion production plant that could go on stream at the turn of the century.

The Chinese leader, who during his trip skirted uncomfortable human rights issues, was due to leave Caracas Thursday evening for Rome where he will attend the World Food Summit hosted by the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO).
